issues.description: The problem statement and the template require an instance method addRating(stars:) (parameter label 'stars'), and the Client in the solution calls addRating(stars:). However, the solution's Course implementation defines the method with a different parameter label (addRating(rating:)). This parameter-label mismatch across artifacts is structural: it will cause compile-time errors or confusion because callers expect the 'stars' label while the solution defines 'rating'.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the parameter label across all artifacts. Preferably change the solution's method signature to match the specification and template: declare the method as 'func addRating(stars: Int)' (or alternatively update the problem statement, template, and Client to use 'rating' consistently). Ensure Client calls and tests use the same label.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect the Course rating method to be called with the external parameter label 'stars' (addRating(stars:)), but the solution's implementation declares the parameter as 'rating' (addRating(rating:)). This mismatch in the external parameter name for the same conceptual operation (adding a star rating to a course) can confuse students when mapping the requirement and template examples to the final implementation and client usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent external parameter label across artifacts. Rename the solution method parameter to match the problem/template signature (func addRating(stars: Int) { ... }) or, if a different internal name is desired, declare both external and internal names consistently (func addRating(stars rating: Int) { ... }) so callers can use addRating(stars:).
